note: 2026-11-03 DAILY BATCH, committed under the chairman's hand before any seat was convened. AUTHORITY: the 2026-11-02 close-out section 5.8(1) authorised, FOR THE NEXT SITTING: 'Fire Rows 1, 2 and 3 unchanged, and do NOT call Row 3 a retry. It is the standing cadence and already authorised, so no new-row price is owed. Re-derive at the sitting's own pin AND NAME THE PIN.' THE CALENDAR IS NOT A DEPARTURE: 5.8 opens 'Next steps for THE NEXT SITTING -- and I name no weekday' and adds 'No seat may write off a calendar day it has not been told is dark.' This sitting IS the next sitting that authorisation names. ROW 3 IS NOT A RETRY and is not described as one: 5.8(1) forbids that reading expressly, and 5.8(4) forbids reading one no_contact as a trend. PIN NAMED, AS 5.8(1) DEMANDS. Measured at pin 3bc5f6a90c5952470a851ed80d9a955042cafe66 (git rev-parse HEAD, identical to origin/main at session open) over 107 files / 777 records of analytics/fetch-results/*.json. UNIT: records. ADMISSION PREDICATE: unquote(url) contains the CaseNo literal AND find is exactly equal to the row's find string. FIRED AND TRUE PUBLISHED SEPARATELY, AS 5.8(2) NOW REQUIRES PERMANENTLY: Row 1 = 10 fired / 10 TRUE; Row 2 = 27 fired / 27 TRUE; Row 3 = 11 fired / 11 TRUE. I OWE 5.8(1) THE IDENTICAL/ABOVE/BELOW DISTINCTION, AND THE ANSWER IS BELOW ON TWO ROWS AND SPLIT ON THE THIRD. 5.8(1) directed me to expect, at session open, Row 1 11 fired / 11 TRUE; Row 2 28 / 28; Row 3 12 fired / 11 TRUE. My figure is ONE BELOW that on Row 1 and Row 2 (both legs), ONE BELOW on Row 3's fired leg, and EQUAL on Row 3's TRUE leg. I say so rather than select the nearest offered word. THE CAUSE IS MEASURED, NOT INFERRED, AND IT IS THE CLOSE-OUT'S ARITHMETIC AND NOT THE INSTRUMENT. At yesterday's pin 81b4060c95ca3511f319a7378afc82ae1504d6bf the corpus was 106 files / 773 records at 9/26/10, which I reproduced by checking that tree out with git archive rather than by copying yesterday's sentence; at my pin it is 107 / 777 at 10/27/11. git diff --name-only between the two pins under analytics/fetch-results/ returns EXACTLY ONE PATH (2026-11-02-daily.json) and the record delta is FOUR, which is yesterday's 3 rows + 1 mandatory control. Each row therefore gains exactly one. 11/28/12 would require yesterday's batch to have contributed TWICE, and it cannot: the merge re-fire OVERWRITES the day's file under the same filename, so a re-fire REPLACES four records and never appends four more. THIS IS THE THIRD CONSECUTIVE SITTING ON WHICH THE SAME RECORD'S MORNING REQUEST NOTE IS RIGHT AND ITS OWN LATER CLOSE-OUT IS WRONG, IN THE SAME DIRECTION, BY ONE, ON EVERY ROW. Yesterday's request note said 'A SUCCESSOR FIRING THESE ROWS AT THE NEXT SITTING SHOULD EXPECT 10/27/11 AND MUST RE-DERIVE RATHER THAN ASSUME IT' -- which is EXACTLY my measured figure -- while the close-out of the same record said 11/28/12. The predecessor diagnosed this split in ITS predecessor, published the diagnosis, and then committed the identical error in its own close-out. It is a defect of hand arithmetic in the close-out, and it is today's optimization item. ROW 3'S FIRED-VERSUS-TRUE DIVERGENCE HAS CLOSED, AND 5.8(1) EXPECTED IT TO PERSIST. Yesterday's section 2.5 recorded the first fired-not-TRUE record in the series' history (a no_contact at status 'timeout'); 5.8(1) accordingly expected Row 3 at 12 fired / 11 TRUE. At my pin Row 3 is 11 / 11: the divergence is NOT in the corpus. Section 7.2 of yesterday's record, written after the merge, predicted exactly this and gave the reason -- the merge re-fire reached the origin at 12:13 and overwrote the 11:31 batch that carried the failure. 7.2 REPRODUCES AT MY PIN AND 5.8(1) DOES NOT; where the two conflict I follow the measurement. STRUCTURAL MEASUREMENT, NOT TEXT MATCH, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS LARGE. A grep for the words 'timeout' and 'no_contact' over analytics/fetch-results/*.json returns 14 and 18 files at my pin, which would read as a contradiction of 7.2's 'zero files contain a timeout'. It is not one. Under the structural predicate (a RECORD whose status or outcome equals 'timeout', or whose outcome equals 'no_contact') the count is ZERO files and ZERO records at my pin; all 18 text hits are in the echoed prose of request notes and row purposes, which is where prior sittings DESCRIBED the failure. 7.2 is confirmed on the predicate that bears the proposition. NO SEAT MAY SETTLE THIS QUESTION BY GREP. THE 11:31 EVIDENCE SURVIVES AND I VERIFIED IT RATHER THAN CITED IT. 7.4 directed a successor wanting what that council saw to read blob b1f7e05418d3e99f5fdf226652e93b157a32dee8 at commit 5712d39a. git cat-file -t returns 'blob' and git cat-file -p parses: fetched_at 2026-11-02T11:31:20Z, requested 3 / completed 2, and the fourth record carries outcome 'no_contact', status 'timeout' (a STRING, not an integer) and NO find_matched key at all. The failure is real, is recoverable, and is recoverable ONLY there. CLONE DEPTH CARRIED ON BOTH LEGS (5.8(6)). git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository returned TRUE at session open at 113 commits; the clone was unshallowed to 2,528; every history-derived and blob-derived figure above is computed after that. 5.8(6) predicted this and the prediction holds for a FOURTH consecutive sitting; the depth is a fact about THIS container and is not inheritable. I DO NOT ADOPT THE 12:13 READING AS THIS COUNCIL'S OBSERVATION, AND 7.3 ASKED ME TO DECIDE AT MY OWN PIN. 7.3 left it to this sitting to 'adopt or decline it at its own pin, with the 12:13 timestamp named.' I DECLINE TO ADOPT IT, for the reason 7.3 itself gave against its own interest: the 2026-11-02T12:13:03Z fetch landed after that sitting's vetting gate closed and no seat examined it. Predicate A at 11 on the committed corpus is nonetheless DEFENSIBLE and I do not call it false -- the record genuinely exists in the run-group -- but this council's own observation of the terminus on 2026-11-02 is the 11:31 batch, which did not reach the chronology cell. Declining is not a finding that the 12:13 reading is wrong. CO-OBSERVATION PRECONDITION, VERIFIED BY ME IN SESSION ON TODAY'S CORPUS before Rows 2 and 3 may be read together: sha256 equality AND byte-length equality between the Row 2 and Row 3 records hold on ELEVEN of eleven same-batch pairs -- 2026-10-23 91a5c03e, -24 bd1f07d0, -25 4ba834ab, -26 8717a789, -27 de7baca3, -28 9b34347c, -29 60627eb5, -30 191f689a, -31 2e0a31fe, 11-01 69064b21, 11-02 90cb04d2 -- each pair identical and each at equal byte length. Yesterday's ten reproduce exactly and 2026-11-02 adds the eleventh, which exists ONLY because of the re-fire I decline to adopt as an observation. PUBLISH NO FAILURE RATE for this precondition: the denominator was withdrawn and restating '1 in 97' repeats a sustained defect. PREDICATE LETTERS BINDING ON THREAD 88: Predicate A (a record in the run-group carries find = 'December 16, 2025 Each party' with find_matched true) stands at 11 on this corpus. PREDICATE B IS NOT PUBLISHED AND NO FIGURE IS OFFERED FOR IT (1101-S11): its executable predicate is unwritten and its selection rule unpublished. A hit on Rows 2 and 3 together today would be the TWELFTH same-batch co-observation. ROW 1 PRE-REGISTRATION, QUOTED IN FULL IN ITS CORRECTED THREE-SENTENCE FORM (the third sentence was dropped without an ellipsis on 2026-10-27, objection 1027-C10): 'The Ring-3 trigger fires on any Latest Development naming a jurisdictional or admissibility event, OR the disappearance of the literal "No References Available", whichever comes first. READ THE FIELD, NOT ONLY THE LITERAL. The continued PRESENCE of that literal is EQUALITY AND IS NOT PROGRESS, and no successor may read it as such.' ROW 3 PRE-REGISTERED NULL MEANING, in the amended 2026-10-25 section 5.2(d) text and not the text first registered (which objection 1025-C4 struck for a silently swapped entity): a null here while Row 2 hits means EITHER the chronology entry moved OR an undecoded HTML entity entered the locus -- NEVER 'the literal is absent'. Named entity ' '; demonstration = the find = 'Procedural Order No. 11' windows at analytics/fetch-results/2026-10-19-daily.json records[4] and 2026-10-22-daily.json records[6]. AND, NEW SINCE 2026-11-02, A THIRD DISJUNCT IS NOW WITNESSED: the row may also fail to reach the origin at all, in which case the relay writes outcome 'no_contact' with NO find_matched key and the row is NOT a null and NOT evidence about the page. COMPANION-CONTROL RULE (analytics/fetch-requests/README.md): the rule fires on a row EXPECTED TO PRODUCE A NULL. All three rows are expected to HIT on the joins above (10/10, 27/27, 11/11 -- every admitted record TRUE on every row), so no row today is expected to null and the rule does not fire. Rows 2 and 3 share a URL in any event, so each is the other's same-stream witness. That is the rule INAPPLICABLE ON ITS OWN TERMS, not waived and not satisfied by accident. PROHIBITION SCREEN, RUN BEFORE THE ROWS WERE WRITTEN rather than after (objection 1021-C18): all three rows are on icsid.worldbank.org, which is on ALLOWED_HOSTS (scripts/fetch_relay.py:48-50); no row touches www.italaw.com, italaw.com, investmentpolicy.unctad.org, unctad.org or any IISD path-family host (standing prohibition); no row requests 'Subject of Dispute' or 'Economic Sector' (thread 34, licence-suspended); no row touches ARB/24/16, ARB/24/45, ARB/22/2 (monthly, next due 2026-11-18), ARB/12/1 or ARB/17/19 (named and not cured, zero budget by design); no fedlex.admin.ch row and nothing touching Swiss SR 0.975.247.2 (escalation 4, Emory's manual query); web.archive.org and travizory.com are NOT requested and both are absent from ALLOWED_HOSTS. NO R-e, NO R2, NO 'Instrument(s) Invoked', NO 'Travizory' party-name row (5.8(9)). NO icsidfiles.worldbank.org PDF ROW -- ground P1, unchanged: content_type == 'application/pdf', 10 records, 10 of 10 at status 200, 0 of 10 with a nonempty excerpt. P1 is the predicate; the '!= text/html' reading is NOT the predicate and cannot bear the proposition. This is the RELAY arm and is distinct from the SEARCH arm named next, which is eligible today. NO NEW ROW, per 5.8(3). Any future row is priced on the ASSEMBLED, STITCHED ON-STATE RUN (2026-09-15 Ruling 1, binding); a no-stitching union figure may not substitute, and where both are computed both are published. No row was designed today, so no price was owed. The second same-run witness row on UNCT/20/6 priced and declined by the analyst on 2026-11-02 STAYS DECLINED and I do not reopen it. THE icsidfiles.worldbank.org allowed_domains SEARCH ARM IS ELIGIBLE TODAY AND ITS SCREEN IS RE-DERIVED AT MY PIN, NOT CARRIED. 2026-10-30 authorised it in principle 'to fire no earlier than Tuesday 2026-11-03', 2026-10-31 section 4 and 2026-11-02 section 5.8(8) both made it eligible '2026-11-03 or later ... re-screened at its own pin on the day'. TODAY IS 2026-11-03. SCREEN RE-RUN BY ME IN SESSION: analytics/search-results/ holds 25 files at my pin and allowed_domains_on_any_call is null on 25 of 25, so the arm is NOVEL; the character-identical string under blocked_domains is held at 2026-10-26.json Q3 and 2026-10-25.json Q3, so the same-string comparator EXISTS, which is the readability condition that ledger entry INSTRUMENT-blocked-domains-efficacy-readable-only-against-the-same-query-string requires. The string, transcribed verbatim from 2026-10-26.json call Q3: ICSID 2026 "Decision on the Respondent's Objection" Rule 41(5) intellectual property patent covered investment upheld. CONFOUND DECLARED BEFORE FIRING, as 2026-10-26's own filter_note declared it: the two arms are EIGHT DAYS and two seat-instances apart and engine result sets are not stable over time, so this is a one-call observation against a stale comparator and NOT a controlled experiment. It is an instrument question, not a topical one. SEARCH BUDGET: ONE, AND IT IS THIS ARM. 5.8(9) set 'Search budget zero, or one if a genuinely new monitored-author surface appears'; no new monitored-author surface has appeared and the Roberts fortnight runs to 2026-11-15, so that conditional does NOT open and the check is not re-fired. The one query authorised today is the icsidfiles allowed_domains arm under its own separate standing authorisation, which is a different authorisation and I do not conflate the two. ZERO BUDGET UNCHANGED on the ARB/25/54 pleaded-asset question; fedlex.admin.ch and Swiss SR 0.975.247.2 in any formulation; ARB/12/1 and ARB/17/19; thread 11 (record only); ARB/22/2 (next due 2026-11-18). INSTRUMENT STATUS MEASURED THIS MORNING, NOT ASSUMED. A neutral-host curl probe to example.com failed 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403', and the gateway's own status endpoint logged that denial for example.com:443 at 2026-11-03T11:15:19Z. The separate fetch service returned ENOTFOUND on the same neutral control (example.com) and again on www.italaw.com. BOTH DIRECT INSTRUMENTS ARE DEAD AND THAT IS NOT A STATE CHANGE; the DNS-resolution failure mode is unchanged from 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-02. This is a fact about this session's plumbing and NEVER a fact about any resource. The relay and the search track are the live instruments, and NOTHING IS STRANDED TODAY FOR WANT OF FETCH. PROVENANCE -- THE CORRECTED CONVENTION, THIRD SITTING. Merging a request file to main is itself a push to analytics/fetch-requests/**, so the merge RE-FIRES this workflow and overwrites analytics/fetch-results/2026-11-03-daily.json with a later run id and fetched_at. THIS RECORD CITES ITS BATCH BY COMMIT AND BLOB, which are immutable and which a re-fire adds to rather than destroys. I make no claim in the form 'X survives the re-fire' about any results file's own sha256: it cannot. I propose no change to scripts/fetch_relay.py or to the workflow -- both are outside this session's merge scope and the question is the operator's. BUDGET: three rows plus the runner's mandatory https://example.com/ control = 4 fetches, under MAX_URLS 12 (scripts/fetch_relay.py:76), leaving eight slots unspent. The spare capacity is blocked by licence, page geometry and sequencing -- not by budget.
